findings.cross_file_justification: The newly declared review-catch-only arms enter the report's component decisions, but the existing primary-metric selection requires a build metric for them.
findings.description: a0_bare_fable, a1_review_only, and a1_no_dissent require hidden_test_pass_rate despite supporting only review-catch tasks. They therefore always receive a missing-primary clause and cannot reach remove or simplify, regardless of their measured review performance.
findings.failure_mode: Complete, valid review-catch experiments produce permanently inconclusive component decisions.
findings.suggested_fix: Define review-catch-only primaries using defect_catch_rate and select that policy for these arms. Verify that complete review-only data can reach the applicable decision outcomes.

findings.description: Excluding eval_only arms from components also excludes a1_full_openmount from detail_arms, while list_reason() does not classify its rows for separate reporting. Its accepted measurements consequently disappear from both the rendered arm results and arms JSON.
findings.failure_mode: An open-mount evaluation batch completes, but the report omits the oracle control needed to inspect the intended A/B comparison.
findings.suggested_fix: Separate decision eligibility from reporting eligibility: retain eval_only arms in detailed results and JSON while excluding them from shipped-default decisions and the component comparison count.

findings.cross_file_justification: The new components filter (diff) adds a0_bare_fable, a1_review_only and a1_no_dissent to `components`; Analysis.primaries() (head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:654-658, untouched) returns [hidden_test_pass_rate, defect_catch_rate] for any arm whose task_types include review-catch, and suites/ablation-2.0.yaml rules.primaries_by_arm (diff-touched file) only has build_only/all_types keys.
findings.description: The three new review-catch-only arms are counted as components (k goes 6 -> 9 in the expected-false-positive sentence) but decide() will always emit `no valid pair (hidden_test_pass_rate)` for them because a review-catch-only arm never has a build-task metric. They can never reach remove/simplify, so the report's k=9 EFP arithmetic describes nine decidable comparisons while three are structurally undecidable, and the suite rules carry no review_only primaries entry for them.
findings.failure_mode: Every batch report emits permanent `no valid pair` decisions for a0_bare_fable/a1_review_only/a1_no_dissent regardless of data, and the Method section's false-positive expectation (9 x (1-level)/2) overstates the number of live tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a review_only key to rules.primaries_by_arm (defect_catch_rate only) and make Analysis.primaries() select it when task_types == [review-catch]; alternatively compute k over arms that have at least one admissible primary, and add a bats case asserting a review-catch-only component can reach `remove`/`keep` from fixture rows.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff removes eval_only arms from `components` but does not route them anywhere else; list_reason()/detail_arms/arms JSON (untouched) have no eval_only branch, so a1_full_openmount rows are ingested into cells and then dropped from every rendered section.
findings.description: a1_full_openmount exists solely as the open-mount oracle A/B against a1_full (suite comment: 'evaluation control'). After this change its rows are parsed, enter cells, and are never listed, decided, or emitted in the arms JSON. The A/B the arm was added to produce is silently never reported, and an operator reading the report cannot tell the arm ran at all.
findings.failure_mode: A batch that spends budget on a1_full_openmount trials yields a report with zero mention of them; the oracle-open vs closed defect_catch_rate comparison is lost and nothing warns about it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit eval_only path in build(): collect eval_only arms, render an 'Evaluation controls (not decision arms)' section with the paired comparison against a1_full on defect_catch_rate, include them in the arms JSON with `eval_only: true`, and have list_reason() return a reason for them so no row is silently discarded. Add a bats assertion that a1_full_openmount rows appear in the report.

findings.cross_file_justification: The four new arms are declared in the diff-touched suite file, but the same file's `priority:` list (head line ~55, untouched) is what run-ablation.sh uses to derive the default --arms set.
findings.description: The new arms are added to `arms` but not to `priority`. run-ablation.sh schedules the default batch from `priority`, so a default `run-ablation.sh --batch ...` with no explicit --arms never launches a0_bare_fable, a1_review_only, a1_no_dissent or a1_full_openmount. The run-ablation.bats case added here passes only because it names --arms a1_full explicitly.
findings.failure_mode: Operators running the documented default batch get no review-catch control trials; the FR-5 arms are dead unless hand-listed every time.
findings.suggested_fix: Append the four arm ids to `priority:` in the intended scheduling position (and, since a1_full_openmount is eval_only, document whether it belongs in the default priority or is opt-in), and add a run-ablation.bats case asserting the default arm set includes them.

findings.description: `jq -r '.eval_only // false'` compared with the string `true` means any non-boolean truthy value (eval_only: "yes", 1, "true ") makes EVAL_ONLY=false and the arm runs unrestricted. validate-suite.sh rejects such values, but pipeline-run.sh does not run the validator, and an operator-edited --suite-file reaches this code directly.
findings.failure_mode: A mis-typed eval_only on the open-mount arm silently drops the batch-context guard the feature exists to enforce.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `jq -e '(.eval_only // false) == true'` for the positive case and `die_usage` when `.eval_only` is present and not a boolean (`jq -e '.eval_only | type != "boolean"'`), mirroring the validator.

findings.description: The dry-run `config_edits=` field is derived by a hand-written jq over four toggles (companion_voice, gates, dissent, flatline). The other nine toggles in the vocabulary (sprint_plan, context_resets, karpathy_block, rule_files, audit_delta_instruction, effort, bare_model, loa_mount, oracle_open) always render as `-`, whether or not lib/sandbox-mount.sh apply_arm_toggles edits .loa.config.yaml for them. The header documents this field as 'the arm's sandbox .loa.config.yaml edits', so for a2_no_sprint_plan / a6_one_window the dry run may claim no config edits while the real run performs some, and any future change to apply_arm_toggles diverges silently.
findings.failure_mode: Operators using --dry-run to confirm what an arm changes in the sandbox get an incomplete or wrong answer with no signal that the field is partial.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose the toggle->config-key mapping from lib/sandbox-mount.sh (e.g. a `plan_arm_toggles <toggles-json>` function used by both apply_arm_toggles and the dry run), or at minimum label the field as covering only the flatline keys and add a bats case for a2/a6 dry runs against the real lib behaviour.

findings.description: LOA_ABLATION_BATCH_CONTEXT=1 is attached only to the run_trial launch command. The pipeline-run.sh refusal fires on every invocation including --dry-run, so any other place run-ablation.sh (or a wrapper) invokes pipeline-run.sh for an arm — a preflight plan print, a retry path that rebuilds the command outside run_trial, or a took-effect re-run — will get exit 2 and no pipeline.json for a1_full_openmount. The RAB-c131-5 test only exercises a1_full, which is not eval_only, so it would not catch such a path.
findings.failure_mode: An eval_only arm scheduled in a batch is refused on a non-run_trial invocation path and surfaces as an interrupted/synthesized trial rather than a clear configuration error.
findings.suggested_fix: Grep run-ablation.sh for every `$PIPELINE_BIN` invocation and set the variable at each, or export it once at the top of the batch/smoke code paths (the header currently promises it is never exported to the runner's shell; if that promise matters, centralise the env prefix in a single `launch_pipeline` helper). Extend RAB-c131-5 to schedule a1_full_openmount through the stub and assert it is launched, not refused.
